cat > what-is-cyrus.md <<'EOF'
---
title: What Cyrus is
category: Start
order: 1
summary: Describe a mod, get a tested, installable one. What Cyrus does and what it does not.
tags: overview, minecraft, about
---
Cyrus is an AI mod studio. You describe a mod in plain language. Cyrus plans it, writes the code, compiles it, scans it, boots it on a real test server and hands you a file you can install.

Today Cyrus builds **Minecraft server mods** (Paper servers). Every other game is **coming soon**. Nothing in Cyrus pretends otherwise.

## What you get
- A mod you can install on a Nxeon game server, or download as a `.jar`.
- Studios to change textures, sounds, 3D models, motion and effects, and settings without writing another prompt. See [the studios](help:studios-overview).
- A Test Flight result on every build, so you know what was actually checked. See [Test Flight](help:test-flight).
- Revisions you can roll back to at any time.

## What Cyrus does not do
- It does not promise that a mod is bug-free. Test Flight boots it and runs checks; it cannot prove every behaviour.
- It does not touch your server unless you connect it and approve each server. See [connecting your account](help:connect-nxeon).
- It does not build for games other than Minecraft yet. See [games and versions](help:games-and-versions).

Ready? Start with [your first mod](help:getting-started).
EOF
cat > getting-started.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Your first mod
category: Start
order: 2
summary: From sign-in to a mod running on your server, step by step.
tags: first mod, quick start, tour
---
This takes a few minutes. You can stop at any step and come back; your project is saved.

1. **Sign in with Nxeon.** Cyrus uses your Nxeon account. One login, one wallet. See [connecting your account](help:connect-nxeon).
2. **Choose New mod.** Pick Minecraft and a server version. Pick a server to install on, or choose to download the jar instead.
3. **Describe it.** Write what you want, or start from a [template](help:templates). Short and specific beats long and vague: see [writing a good prompt](help:writing-a-good-prompt).
4. **Check the cost.** Before you build, Cyrus shows how many tokens the build may hold. It spends only what it uses. See [how spend is shown](help:how-spend-is-shown).
5. **Build and watch.** You see the plan, the code and any assets appear as they are made. A build that fails on our side gives its tokens back.
6. **Read the Test Flight result.** On the project page, check what was booted and tested. See [Test Flight](help:test-flight).
7. **Install.** Install on a connected server, or download the jar. You can roll back at any time. See [installing and rolling back](help:installing-and-rolling-back).

## If you want to change something
Describe the change in the studio chat, or open a studio and edit it by hand. Every change is a new revision, so nothing is lost.

## First-run tour
The first time you open Cyrus, a short tour points out New mod, Projects, Plan and tokens, Your servers and Account. Replay it any time from Account.
EOF
cat > writing-a-good-prompt.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Writing a good prompt
category: Start
order: 3
summary: What to say, what to leave out, and how to ask for changes.
tags: prompt, tips, examples
---
Cyrus builds what you describe. The more concrete the description, the closer the result.

## Say what it does, not how to code it
- Good: "A /heal command that fully heals the player. 60 second cooldown per player. Operators can heal others with /heal <name>."
- Weak: "Healing plugin."

## Include these when they matter
- **Commands** and who may use them (everyone, operators).
- **Numbers**: cooldowns, chances, prices, amounts. Say which should be editable in `config.yml`.
- **What is saved** between restarts (balances, homes, streaks).
- **What players see**: titles, action bar messages, menus, boss bars.
- **Limits**: "only in the overworld", "not in protected zones".

## Keep it to one idea per mod
One clear mod builds better than ten loosely related ones. For a large project, build the core first and add to it. If the mod grows large, see [Mod Packs and modules](help:mod-packs-and-modules).

## Check before you send
Cyrus checks your prompt first. If it is too vague or asks for something it cannot build, it says why and what to change, before any tokens are held.

## Asking for changes
Be specific about the change and leave the rest alone: "Make the cooldown 30 seconds and show it in the action bar." Do not re-describe the whole mod.

## What Cyrus cannot build
Cyrus targets Paper servers on the Minecraft versions it lists. It cannot make client-side mods, and it cannot change the game itself. See [games and versions](help:games-and-versions).

Need ideas? Browse the [templates](help:templates).
EOF
cat > templates.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Starting from a template
category: Start
order: 4
summary: Pick a starter, edit the prompt, build.
tags: templates, examples, starters
---
Templates are example prompts for common Minecraft mods. Each shows what it makes, which studios it uses and which plan it expects.

## How to use one
1. Open **New mod** and choose a category under **Start from a template**.
2. Click a template. Its prompt fills the box.
3. Change anything you like. The template is only a starting point.
4. Check the cost, then build.

## Reading a template card
- **Idea**: what the mod does in one line.
- **Plan**: the lowest plan that fits. Some templates use sound, textures or 3D, which need a plan that includes that studio.
- **Studios and assets**: what the build may create and what you can edit afterwards.
- **Version notes**: anything that differs by Minecraft version.

Templates are written to build on the Minecraft versions Cyrus supports today. They are not guaranteed to build exactly the same every time: the prompt is the specification, and you can change it.
EOF
cat > studios-overview.md <<'EOF'
---
title: The studios
category: Studios
order: 5
summary: Edit textures, sounds, 3D models, motion and settings without another prompt.
tags: studios, texture, sound, model, motion, config
---
A studio is a full-page editor for one part of your mod. Studios edit the same project your builds create. Every save is a revision, and a later build keeps your edits.

| Studio | What you edit | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| [Texture Studio](help:texture-studio) | Item and block art, animated textures | Yakko |
| [Sound Studio](help:sound-studio) | Sound effects for items, mobs and events | Saka and up |
| [Model Studio](help:model-studio) | 3D models, painting, rigs | Yakko |
| [Motion and effects](help:motion-and-effects) | Animation states, effects, presets | See the article |
| [Config and Stats Studio](help:config-studio) | Numbers and settings | Not plan-gated |
| [Designers](help:designers) | Items and abilities, menus, quests, bosses, HUDs | Not plan-gated |

## Plans gate creating, not keeping
Plans decide who can **create or change** an asset in a studio. Installing a mod, keeping it, rebuilding it unchanged and exporting it are never locked. If you drop to a lower plan, what you made still works. See [plans and tokens](help:plans-and-tokens).

## Only what your game can use
A studio or tool is hidden when the game or version cannot use it. If you wonder why something is missing, the page says why.

## On a phone
Studios are built for a desktop screen. On a phone you can view and install; editing is on desktop.
EOF
cat > texture-studio.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Texture Studio
category: Studios
order: 6
summary: A pixel editor for the art in your mod, with AI edits you can accept or reject.
tags: texture, pixel art, items, style
---
Texture Studio edits the item, block and effect textures in your mod. It needs a plan that includes it (Yakko).

## What you can do
- Paint pixel by pixel with layers, undo, palettes and ramps.
- Preview the texture on the item in the places it appears: hotbar, hand, dropped, item frame, head.
- Scrub item states such as idle, pull, aim and reload, where the item has them.
- Apply a **style** across the whole mod so the art matches (palette, outline, noise).
- Ask for an AI edit. It arrives as a **candidate** next to your texture, with a before and after. You accept it or discard it. It never replaces your work on its own.
- Search the texture library and drop an asset in. See [libraries](help:libraries).

## Quality review
The review screen checks palette size, contrast, edges, banding and transparency, and says what to fix.

## Your own game files
If you want to start from the game's own textures, you can bring your own copy. Cyrus reads it in your browser and sends only fingerprints, keeps the file only as long as the job needs, and never contributes it to the library. See [safety and licensing](help:safety-and-licensing).

## Limits
- Older Minecraft versions show fewer item looks. On 1.21.1 only some items can carry a custom look, and the studio shows each limit.
- Cyrus checks that your art is not a near copy of a vanilla texture.
EOF
cat > sound-studio.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Sound Studio
category: Studios
order: 7
summary: Shape the sound of your items, mobs and events.
tags: sound, audio, ogg
---
Sound Studio edits sound effects in your mod. It needs Saka or a higher plan.

## What you can do
- Edit a waveform: trim, fade, gain, pitch, layer sounds, and read loudness.
- Search the sound library by tag, or build a sound from presets.
- Give an item or mob its own sound set for the events it has.
- Write **subtitle keys** so the sound shows as a caption.
- Preview the sound before you build. Edits are non-destructive: your original stays.

## How sounds are exported
Sounds are exported as mono Ogg Vorbis. Mono sounds are positional: they get quieter with distance, like vanilla.

## Your sounds stay yours
New sound keys belong to your mod. Cyrus never overrides a vanilla sound key for the whole server, so other mods and the base game are not changed.

## What the library includes
The library contains sounds that are cleared for use in your mods. Some sound sets are not available to customers yet and show as unavailable. A build then uses a generated sound instead.

Related: [libraries](help:libraries), [safety and licensing](help:safety-and-licensing).
EOF
cat > model-studio.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Model Studio (3D)
category: Studios
order: 8
summary: View, paint and edit the 3D models in your mod.
tags: 3d, model, paint, rig, cuboid
---
Model Studio works on the 3D models in your mod. It needs a plan that includes it (Yakko).

## Layers
1. **Viewport and paint.** Orbit the model, paint on it, and preview it in motion.
2. **Cuboid and bone editor.** Move, resize and rig the parts, and set up animation keys on a timeline.
3. **Mesh retexture.** Light edits and retexturing on a mesh. Export of full meshes is **not available**: Minecraft uses cuboid models, and Cyrus does not convert arbitrary meshes into them.

## Good to know
- Your edits are saved as drafts and survive later builds. If both a build and you changed the same part, your change wins.
- A model is checked against what Minecraft can show before you build.
- What a model looks like in the game client depends on the client. Cyrus checks structure and loading on a test server; it cannot show you a screenshot from a real client yet.

Related: [Motion and effects](help:motion-and-effects), [libraries](help:libraries).
EOF

title: Motion and effects

order: 9
summary: Animation states, particles and effect presets for your items and mobs.
tags: motion, animation, effects, particles, presets

cat > writing-a-good-prompt.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Writing a good prompt
category: Start
order: 3
summary: What to say, what to leave out, and how to ask for changes.
tags: prompt, tips, examples
---
Cyrus builds what you describe. The more concrete the description, the closer the result.

## Say what it does, not how to code it
- Good: "A /heal command that fully heals the player. 60 second cooldown per player. Operators can heal others with /heal <name>."
- Weak: "Healing plugin."

## Include these when they matter
- **Commands** and who may use them (everyone, operators).
- **Numbers**: cooldowns, chances, prices, amounts. Say which should be editable in `config.yml`.
- **What is saved** between restarts (balances, homes, streaks).
- **What players see**: titles, action bar messages, menus, boss bars.
- **Limits**: "only in the overworld", "not in protected zones".

## Keep it to one idea per mod
One clear mod builds better than ten loosely related ones. For a large project, build the core first and add to it. If the mod grows large, see [Mod Packs and modules](help:mod-packs-and-modules).

## Check before you send
Cyrus checks your prompt first. If it is too vague or asks for something it cannot build, it says why and what to change, before any tokens are held.

## Asking for changes
Be specific about the change and leave the rest alone: "Make the cooldown 30 seconds and show it in the action bar." Do not re-describe the whole mod.

## What Cyrus cannot build
Cyrus targets Paper servers on the Minecraft versions it lists. It cannot make client-side mods, and it cannot change the game itself. See [games and versions](help:games-and-versions).

Need ideas? Browse the [templates](help:templates).
EOF

---
title: Libraries
category: Studios

Open the library from a studio or a project. Search by words or tags, preview an asset, and choose **Use in project**. The asset is copied into your project and stays there. Which assets you can use depends on your plan: the Sound Library comes with Saka and up, the Texture Library with Yakko.

Everything in the community library is **CC0**: free to use, no credit needed. Cyrus does not include assets that need attribution. Each entry shows its licence tier and the game versions it fits.

If an asset is taken down, **your mod keeps its own copy** and keeps working. You are told if something you used was removed.

## Sharing your own
Assets you make in a studio can be added to the library after they pass the filters. See [safety and licensing](help:safety-and-licensing). Your Account page shows what you contributed and its state: published, in review, held or removed.

## Not everything is here yet
Some collections are waiting for licence checks and are not available. They are not shown rather than shown and blocked. Coverage is largest for Minecraft; other games are coming soon.

---
title: Rollover and free tokens
category: Plans and tokens
order: 14
summary: Unused plan tokens roll over while you stay subscribed. Nxeon game servers come with free tokens.
tags: rollover, free tokens, servers, renewals, expiry
---
## Rollover
**Unused tokens roll over every month for as long as your plan stays active.** You do not lose last month's tokens when a new month starts.

Good to know:
- A rollover limit may apply. If it does, the Plans tab shows it before you hit it.
- If you cancel or your plan lapses, your plan tokens **pause for a grace period**. Resubscribe within it and they are yours again. After it, they expire. The length of the period is shown on the Plans tab.
- Top-up tokens follow their own expiry, shown next to your balance.

## Free tokens with your servers
**Every paid Nxeon game server you deploy comes with free Cyrus tokens, plus more on each renewal.**
- Only servers for games Cyrus builds for earn them. Today that is Minecraft.
- The amount, any per-server cap, and which servers count are set by Nxeon and can change. Your balance shows where each batch came from.
- If you delete a server or it is refunded soon after you got the tokens, the free tokens for it can be taken back. You are never charged for that: only unspent tokens are reversed.

## Which tokens are spent first
Tokens that expire soonest are used first, so less goes to waste.

Related: [how spend is shown](help:how-spend-is-shown), [plans and tokens](help:plans-and-tokens).
EOF
cat > how-spend-is-shown.md <<'EOF'
---
title: How spend is shown
category: Plans and tokens
order: 15
summary: The live meter during a build, and the totals per mod, version and asset.
tags: spend, meter, estimate, usage, cost
---
Cyrus shows the cost three times: before, during and after.

## Before
On **New mod**, the cost panel shows a range in tokens for the model you chose and the size of mod you described. It is an estimate. It is also the most the build may **hold** while it runs.

## During
The build screen has a live meter:
- **Estimated so far**: what the build has used up to now.
- **Held**: the amount set aside for this build.

## After
When the build ends, the meter settles into one of:
- **Settled**: what the build actually used. The rest of the hold is released.
- **Returned**: tokens given back, for example when a build fails on our side.

---
title: What Cyrus can and cannot do on your server
category: Connect

tags: grants, permissions, revoke, consent, security

When you connect a server, you grant Cyrus a short list of permissions for that server only.

## What Cyrus can do
- **See the server**: name, game, version, status, resources and player count.
- **See installed plugins and mods**: names and versions, to check for conflicts before a build or install.
- **Write mods and config**: only into the plugin, mod, config, data pack and resource pack folders, and only over the exact file it expects.
- **Reload or restart the server** after an install, within a daily limit.
- **Read recent logs**: the end of the console, to check an install worked.
- **Set the resource pack** in the server settings.

## What Cyrus cannot do
- It has no access to your Nxeon password, SSH keys or server login.
- It cannot touch servers you did not tick.
- It cannot write outside the folders above, or overwrite a file it did not expect.
- It cannot run console commands, change your billing, delete a server, or read your wallet.
- It cannot restart a server as often as it likes: restarts are limited.

## Every action is recorded
Each action is tied to you, the server and the grant. Nxeon keeps an audit trail.

## Revoking
Open **Account**, then **Connected servers**, and choose **Disconnect** on a server. All permissions for it end at once. You can reconnect later.

If you revoke while an install is running, Cyrus keeps one narrow ability: **to roll back** what it was installing, so the server is not left half-changed.

Related: [installing and rolling back](help:installing-and-rolling-back).

---
title: Installing and rolling back
category: Install

summary: Put a build on your server, or download it, and go back to any earlier version.
tags: install, rollback, jar, restart, revisions
---
## Install
On the project page, use **Install**:
1. Choose a connected server marked Ready.
2. Cyrus runs a **conflict check** against what is already on the server, including mods you added by hand. A duplicate blocks the install and says which one.
3. Confirm any plan notes shown.
4. Install. If the server is busy or starting, the install is **queued** and runs when it is ready.
5. The result tells you whether the server restarted or needs a restart to load the mod.

You can also **download the jar** and install it yourself.

## What happens behind the scenes
An install is a journaled change. Cyrus makes a backup, writes the files in a staging step, and only then switches over. If a step fails, it undoes the install.

You will see one of these results: installed, queued, rolled back, or **rollback incomplete** (see below).

## Roll back
Every build and revision stays in the project. On the Builds card, choose **Roll back to this** on an earlier build and install it. Uninstalling removes the mod and restores what was there before.

If a rollback cannot finish, the result says **rollback incomplete** and lists what is left. It never reports success it did not achieve. See [troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting).

## When the game updates
If your server moves to a new Minecraft version, Cyrus marks mods built for the old one as **outdated** and notifies you. Rebuild for the new version.

Related: [Test Flight](help:test-flight), [Mod Packs](help:mod-packs-and-modules).
EOF
cat > test-flight.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Test Flight and "boot-tested"
category: Install
order: 20
summary: What Test Flight runs, what its labels mean, and what it cannot tell you.
tags: test flight, boot-tested, verification, quality
---
After a build, Cyrus can run **Test Flight**: a disposable server of your exact Minecraft version, started from scratch.

## What it does
1. Starts a fresh server on the version your mod targets.
2. Loads your mod and checks it enabled.
3. Runs commands against it and checks the responses and the log.
4. Where the mod has tests, runs a scripted test player.
5. Shuts the server down cleanly.

## What the labels mean
- **Flight passed**: every required step ran and passed.
- **Flight failed**: a step ran and failed. The result lists which.
- **Flight incomplete**: a required step did not run. This is never shown as a pass.
- **In flight**: still running.
- **Boot-tested** is shown only for versions and parts where the test actually ran. If a check was skipped, it is listed as skipped.

## What it cannot tell you
- It does not use a real game client. How things look and sound in the client can differ from what was checked.
- Player-behaviour tests currently cover limited versions. Where a check did not run, the result says so.
- A pass means the mod loaded and did what was checked. It is not a guarantee there are no bugs.

## Install gate
Depending on settings, an install can be blocked when a flight fails. The page shows why.

Related: [installing and rolling back](help:installing-and-rolling-back).

title: Mod Packs and modules
category: Install

summary: Install several mods as one unit, or build one big mod out of modules.
tags: mod packs, modules, conflicts, suites
status: pending
---
There are two ways to deal with more than one piece. They are different.

## Mod Packs: several separate mods
A Mod Pack is a set of separate mods that install and roll back **as one unit**.
- Cyrus checks the whole set for conflicts first (duplicate commands, shared files, version clashes).
- **Every open warning must be acknowledged** before you can install.
- Mod Packs can include third-party mods by link and checksum. Cyrus only embeds mods it built itself.
- Not locked behind a plan.
- Uninstalling or rolling back removes the whole pack.

## Modules: one big mod made of parts
For a large mod, you can split it into **modules** inside one mod. It stays one mod with one jar, but you can:
- edit or rebuild one module without touching the others,
- see each module's own revisions, tests and token spend,
- see which modules depend on which, and get an error if they do not fit together,
- export a module as a mod of its own.

> Modules are **not available yet**. They are built and being finalised. This page will update when they are switched on.

## Which should I use?
- Different authors or separate ideas: **Mod Pack**.
- One large idea you want to build in pieces: **modules**.

## Builds are scanned
Every build is compiled and scanned before it can be installed. Builds that fail the scan are not installable.

## The library licence
The shared library only contains **CC0** assets, free for anyone to use with no credit. Cyrus does not use assets that need attribution.

## Sharing your assets
Assets you create in a studio can be **contributed automatically** after they pass the filters. When this happens you can see it under Library contributions on your dashboard, with its state: published, in review, held or removed.

By using Cyrus you agree to the licence set out in the Terms for assets you contribute. Read the Terms for the exact wording.

### What is never contributed
- Anything you **upload or import**.
- Anything derived from another file, including game files you bring.
- Content from templates.
- Anything that fails a filter.
- Your mod's code and settings. The library holds assets only.

### What the filters check
Trademarks, names of real weapons, and violent, extremist, drug-related and adult content. Assets that might match are **held** for review rather than published.

## Reporting
See [reporting and takedowns](help:reporting-and-takedowns).

## Game files
Game files are the game maker's. If you bring your own, Cyrus uses them only for your job, does not keep them longer than needed, and never shares them. See [Texture Studio](help:texture-studio).
EOF

The Cyrus API lets your own tools and scripts do what the app does.

1. Choose a connected server marked Ready.
2. Cyrus runs a **conflict check** against what is already on the server, including mods you added by hand. A duplicate blocks the install and says which one.
3. Confirm any plan notes shown.
4. Install. If the server is busy or starting, the install is **queued** and runs when it is ready.
5. The result tells you whether the server restarted or needs a restart to load the mod.

You can also **download the jar** and install it yourself.

## What happens behind the scenes
An install is a journaled change. Cyrus makes a backup, writes the files in a staging step, and only then switches over. If a step fails, it undoes the install.

You will see one of these results: installed, queued, rolled back, or **rollback incomplete** (see below).

## Roll back
Every build and revision stays in the project. On the Builds card, choose **Roll back to this** on an earlier build and install it. Uninstalling removes the mod and restores what was there before.

If a rollback cannot finish, the result says **rollback incomplete** and lists what is left. It never reports success it did not achieve. See [troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting).

## When the game updates
If your server moves to a new Minecraft version, Cyrus marks mods built for the old one as **outdated** and notifies you. Rebuild for the new version.

Related: [Test Flight](help:test-flight), [Mod Packs](help:mod-packs-and-modules).
EOF
cat > test-flight.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Test Flight and "boot-tested"
category: Install
order: 20
summary: What Test Flight runs, what its labels mean, and what it cannot tell you.
tags: test flight, boot-tested, verification, quality
---
After a build, Cyrus can run **Test Flight**: a disposable server of your exact Minecraft version, started from scratch.

## What it does
1. Starts a fresh server on the version your mod targets.
2. Loads your mod and checks it enabled.
3. Runs commands against it and checks the responses and the log.
4. Where the mod has tests, runs a scripted test player.
5. Shuts the server down cleanly.

## What the labels mean
- **Flight passed**: every required step ran and passed.
- **Flight failed**: a step ran and failed. The result lists which.
- **Flight incomplete**: a required step did not run. This is never shown as a pass.
- **In flight**: still running.
- **Boot-tested** is shown only for versions and parts where the test actually ran. If a check was skipped, it is listed as skipped.

## What it cannot tell you
- It does not use a real game client. How things look and sound in the client can differ from what was checked.
- Player-behaviour tests currently cover limited versions. Where a check did not run, the result says so.
- A pass means the mod loaded and did what was checked. It is not a guarantee there are no bugs.

## Install gate
Depending on settings, an install can be blocked when a flight fails. The page shows why.

Related: [installing and rolling back](help:installing-and-rolling-back).
EOF
cat > mod-packs-and-modules.md <<'EOF'
---
title: Mod Packs and modules
category: Install
order: 21
summary: Install several mods as one unit, or build one big mod out of modules.
tags: mod packs, modules, conflicts, suites
status: pending
---
There are two ways to deal with more than one piece. They are different.

## Mod Packs: several separate mods
A Mod Pack is a set of separate mods that install and roll back **as one unit**.
- Cyrus checks the whole set for conflicts first (duplicate commands, shared files, version clashes).
- **Every open warning must be acknowledged** before you can install.
- Mod Packs can include third-party mods by link and checksum. Cyrus only embeds mods it built itself.
- Not locked behind a plan.
- Uninstalling or rolling back removes the whole pack.

## Modules: one big mod made of parts
For a large mod, you can split it into **modules** inside one mod. It stays one mod with one jar, but you can:
- edit or rebuild one module without touching the others,
- see each module's own revisions, tests and token spend,
- see which modules depend on which, and get an error if they do not fit together,
- export a module as a mod of its own.

> Modules are **not available yet**. They are built and being finalised. This page will update when they are switched on.

## Which should I use?
- Different authors or separate ideas: **Mod Pack**.
- One large idea you want to build in pieces: **modules**.
EOF

---
title: Troubleshooting
category: Install

summary: Common problems and what to do next.
tags: troubleshooting, errors, help, build failed, install failed
---
## My build failed
Open the build. It says what stopped and what was charged. Cyrus already tried to repair it. Then:
- If it says the request cannot be built, adjust the prompt as suggested.
- If it says our side failed, try again. You are not charged for our failures.
- Still stuck? Use **Get help** on the build page. It sends the build with your message.

## It says I do not have enough tokens
Check the estimate on New mod. Top up, switch to a smaller model for a simple mod, or wait for your plan tokens. See [plans and tokens](help:plans-and-tokens).

## A studio is locked
The studio needs a higher plan. Open **See plans**. Your existing work is never locked.

## My server is not listed, or says not ready
- The server must be a Minecraft server on your Nxeon account, and it must be running.
- Only Paper servers can take an install.
- If you just connected it, refresh.
See [connecting your account](help:connect-nxeon).

## Install failed or says rollback incomplete
Nothing is left half-installed without the result telling you. Read what is listed, then try again or roll back to the previous build. If it still says incomplete, send us the project link through Get help.

## The mod is installed but does nothing
- Restart the server if the result said a restart is needed.
- Check the server version against the mod's version. Rebuild if it says outdated.
- Check for another plugin with the same command name.

## Test Flight says incomplete
A required check did not run. It is not a failure of your mod. Run it again, or install anyway if the page allows it.

## I cannot sign in
Use the same Nxeon account. Your Nxeon email must be verified. If sign-in loops, clear cookies for cyrus.my and try again.
EOF

---
title: Safety and licensing
category: Safety
order: 23
summary: How builds are scanned, what the library licence is, and what is never shared.
tags: safety, licence, library, contribution, cc0, filters
---
## Builds are scanned
Every build is compiled and scanned before it can be installed. Builds that fail the scan are not installable.

## The library licence
The shared library only contains **CC0** assets, free for anyone to use with no credit. Cyrus does not use assets that need attribution.

## Sharing your assets
Assets you create in a studio can be **contributed automatically** after they pass the filters. When this happens you can see it under Library contributions on your dashboard, with its state: published, in review, held or removed.

By using Cyrus you agree to the licence set out in the Terms for assets you contribute. Read the Terms for the exact wording.

### What is never contributed
- Anything you **upload or import**.
- Anything derived from another file, including game files you bring.
- Content from templates.
- Anything that fails a filter.
- Your mod's code and settings. The library holds assets only.

### What the filters check
Trademarks, names of real weapons, and violent, extremist, drug-related and adult content. Assets that might match are **held** for review rather than published.

## Reporting
See [reporting and takedowns](help:reporting-and-takedowns).

## Game files
Game files are the game maker's. If you bring your own, Cyrus uses them only for your job, does not keep them longer than needed, and never shares them. See [Texture Studio](help:texture-studio).
EOF

Use **Report** on a library entry or mod page. Choose a reason and add a note. Reports are reviewed by people. Several reports on the same item hold it until reviewed.

## Copyright notices
If you own something and it is in the library or on a mod page, open a Nxeon support ticket marked **Copyright notice**. Include what was used, where, and proof you own it. Cyrus removes the item while the case is reviewed.

---
title: Privacy and your data
category: Account
order: 25
summary: What Cyrus keeps, how to export it, and how to delete it.
tags: privacy, data, export, delete, gdpr
---
## What Cyrus keeps
- Your account link to Nxeon (your Nxeon user, not a separate password).
- Your projects, builds, revisions and assets.
- Your token and plan history.
- What you contributed to the library.
- Records of installs and which servers you granted.

Your prompts and mod are processed by AI models to build the mod. They are not used to train models for other people. 

## Export your data
Open **Account**, then **Data**, and choose **Export**. We prepare a zip of your projects and account records. You get a notification when it is ready, and a download link for a limited time.

## Delete your data
Choose **Delete** in the same place. Your request waits for a short grace period so you can cancel. After that your account data is erased.
- Assets already **published in the library** stay, with your name removed.
- Records we must keep for billing and legal reasons are kept.

## Notifications
You choose what Cyrus emails you under **Account**, then **Notifications**. Takedown notices are always sent.

## Cookies and analytics
Optional analytics and ad tracking only run after you accept them in the consent banner.

See also [connecting your account](help:connect-nxeon).
EOF
cat > api-keys-and-the-api.md <<'EOF'
---
title: API keys and the API
category: Account
order: 26
summary: Create a key, choose what it can do, and call the Cyrus API.
tags: api, keys, developers, webhooks
---
The Cyrus API lets your own tools and scripts do what the app does.

## Create a key
Open **Account**, then **API keys**, and choose **Create key**. Give it a name and tick the permissions it needs.
- The key is shown **once**. Copy it then. Cyrus stores only a fingerprint and cannot show it again.
- Keys can be revoked at any time. Revoke a key if you think it leaked.
- Give a key the smallest set of permissions that works.

## Permissions
Read projects, change projects, read builds, **start builds (spends tokens)**, read and request installs, search the catalog, change mod settings, contribute to the library, read account and token balance.

## Calling the API
Send the key as a bearer token on requests to the versioned API. Requests that start a build or install take an idempotency key, so a retry never builds twice. Builds started by API use your tokens and your plan, with the same limits as the app.

## What exists today
Reading and creating projects, starting and reading builds, installing and reading installs, changing mod settings, searching the catalog, and contributing library assets. More operations are planned and listed in the API reference as such. Webhooks for build and install results are being rolled out.

## Limits
Keys are rate limited. Calls that exceed the limit get a clear error with when to retry.

Related: [plans and tokens](help:plans-and-tokens).
EOF

content.thinking:
I should be honest that resource pack loading hasn't actually been verified in a real game client yet, only on test servers. I'll add a note to the texture studio limits section clarifying that confirmation in a live client is still pending.

I also need to vary template notes per version — custom item looks are limited on 1.21.1 (vanilla carrier damage states only) but get real item model definitions on 1.21.4+; dialog menus need 1.21.8+ (else fall back to chest menus, which is what templates use); and animated creatures are preview-only on 26.x, not buildable yet, so I'll just mention that in notes rather than offering it as a starter template. For template categories, I'm considering extending beyond the existing set (Admin, Economy, Gameplay, Social, World) to add Items and Atmosphere for sound/effects content.

I want to keep the 12 existing templates with their same ids so prompts persist, enriching them, and add 12 new ones for 24 total. The tricky part is plan requirements: a template's expected plan should be the max of its model tier and any asset-creation needs, since builds alone don't require studio access but creating custom textures or sounds does — so a template needing custom sound requires Saka+ even if the model tier is Katara, and custom textures/models push it to Yakko. Each template will also carry a studios-used array listing which studio types it touches.

I'm now drafting the 12 new templates: an ember wand with custom texture and fireball ability (Yakko), a lifesteal sword and grappling hook (Saka, code-only), a vein miner enchant, death chest/grave system, player warps with TPA cooldowns, a server rules/first-join book, and an auto-restart announcer with scheduled countdown broadcasts, mostly landing at Katara or Saka tiers depending on whether they need custom assets.

I'm also weighing jobs and auction house systems as Yakko-tier for their complexity, ambient cave sounds and particle trails as Saka-tier atmosphere features needing sound/particle work, and world features like treasure hunts, day/night voting, teleport pads, and floating damage numbers—settling on a final list of twelve that balances categories and asset complexity.

Tallying it up, I land on ember-wand, lifesteal-sword, grappling-hook, vein-miner, graves, tpa, rules-book, announcer, jobs, auction, ambient-sounds, and particle-trails as my twelve new additions, dropping treasure-hunt to keep the count right. Combined with the twelve existing features, I'm now checking the category balance across Admin, Social, World, Gameplay, Economy, Items, and Atmosphere to make sure nothing's too lopsided.

Now I'm mapping each feature to its model/studio assignment based on the existing pattern (katara, saka, yakko), noting things like boss using the boss bar and streak using welcome titles, and planning how shop and quests tie into the menus designer. I'm also drafting per-feature version compatibility notes, like confirming titles work via the Paper title API across all supported versions and detailing how the ember-wand's item model differs between 1.21.4+ and 1.21.1.

I'm deciding to avoid speculative version notes—only stating facts I actually know, like sound behavior or menu types, and defaulting to a neutral "no version-specific notes" phrasing for anything unverified rather than claiming untested compatibility.

For the new-mod flow, I want example prompts rotating as placeholders plus a handful of clickable "ideas" chips that let users set the prompt directly, keeping this lightweight by using the first few examples deterministically rather than random selection. I'm also weighing whether to keep the templates file as-is or restructure it as a re-export from a new content module while preserving the existing exported names.

I'm extending the template data to around 24 enriched entries plus expanded categories, editing the file in place rather than splitting it out. For the UI, selecting a template should show a plan pill on the card and a small details panel listing studios, assets, and version notes, keeping everything minimal and honest about relying only on the Paper API -- including writing clear, plain descriptions for custom texture prompts like the Yakko-style ones.

- Translations: all copy is English only.

# Support macros for Cyrus (r50)

Twenty canned replies for Nxeon support staff. They are **drafts**: read the ticket, check the "Look at" line, fill the `{{placeholders}}`, and only send after a person has approved the reply. Never auto-send. Speak as Nxeon: Cyrus is a Nxeon product, so there is no outside provider to mention.

Where to look: **Support context** panel on the ticket (the build, its Test Flight result, the plan and token state), `/admin/cyrus` Builds, Users and tokens, Reconciliation, and Library moderation. Customer help articles to link are in the [help center](../../../content/cyrus/help/). Every article name below is a help article slug under `/help/<slug>` on cyrus.my.

Rules for every reply: say what happened, say whether anything was charged or changed, say what happens next. No promises about dates. No token or price figures unless you read them from the account. Legal macros (12 to 14) need the owner or a lawyer to approve the wording before first use.

Placeholders: `{{name}}` first name, `{{project}}` mod name, `{{build}}` build or project link, `{{server}}` server name, `{{n}}` a figure you read from the account.

---

## 1. Build failed on our side
**Look at:** build error code (`unavailable`, `ai_unavailable`, `interrupted`, `timeout`); whether tokens were returned (ledger).
> Hi {{name}},
> Your build of {{project}} stopped because of a problem on our side, not because of your prompt. {{n}} tokens that the build held have been returned to your balance, and nothing was charged for it.
> You can start it again from {{build}}. If it fails the same way twice, reply here and we will look at it directly.
> Nxeon Support

## 2. Build failed because the request cannot be built
**Look at:** error code `compile`, `safety`, `refused`, `budget`.
> Hi {{name}},
> The build of {{project}} could not finish. {{reason}}
> What usually helps: ask for fewer features at once and add the rest as changes afterwards; avoid other plugins (Cyrus builds on plain Paper); split a very large idea into two or three mods. Our guide on writing a good prompt has examples: /help/writing-a-good-prompt.
> If you tell us what you wanted the mod to do, we can suggest how to word it.
> Nxeon Support

## 3. My tokens are missing or the balance looks wrong
**Look at:** Users and tokens (lots, ledger, reservations), Reconciliation. Held tokens look "missing" while a build runs.
> Hi {{name}},
> We checked your Cyrus balance. Here is what we see: {{summary: available, held by running builds, last purchases and builds}}.
> Tokens held by a running build come back when it ends, minus what it used. Your build page shows the settled amount for each build. How spend is shown: /help/how-spend-is-shown.
> If a figure still looks wrong, tell us which build or date and we will go through it line by line.
> Nxeon Support

## 4. Tokens expired, or a rollover question
**Look at:** plan active? lapse or grace state, lot expiry dates. Do not quote numbers you have not read.
> Hi {{name}},
> Unused plan tokens roll over every month for as long as your plan stays active. {{If lapsed: Your plan lapsed on {{date}}, so your plan tokens are paused for a grace period. If you resubscribe in time they come back.}} {{If expired: They passed the end of that period and have expired.}}
> Top-up tokens follow their own expiry, which is shown next to your balance. More detail: /help/token-rollover-and-free-tokens.
> Nxeon Support

## 5. I did not get free tokens with my server
**Look at:** the server's game (only games Cyrus builds for earn them: Minecraft), purchase or renewal event, per-server cap, early-delete reversal.
> Hi {{name}},
> Free Cyrus tokens come with paid Nxeon game servers for games Cyrus builds for, and more on each renewal. For {{server}} we see: {{reason: granted on {{date}} / not eligible because it is not a Minecraft server / reversed because the server was deleted soon after / the per-server limit was reached}}.
> {{If eligible but missing: We have added them now.}} Your balance shows where each batch came from.
> Nxeon Support

## 6. Refund request (plan or top-up)
**Look at:** the purchase, how many tokens were spent. Refund decisions follow Nxeon billing policy; the owner approves exceptions.
> Hi {{name}},
> Thanks for getting in touch about {{purchase}}. {{Decision.}}
> If a purchase is refunded, the unspent tokens from it are removed. Tokens already spent on builds are not returned. Your mods and installs keep working either way.
> Nxeon Support

## 7. I paid but no tokens or plan arrived
**Look at:** Reconciliation (plan drift, dead webhooks), Stripe payment status, the two-sided entitlement view. Replay a dead webhook if one is stuck.
> Hi {{name}},
> We found your payment of {{date}} and {{what we did: credited the tokens / re-sent the plan update}}. Your balance should now show {{n}} tokens and your plan as {{plan}}. Please refresh Cyrus.
> We are sorry for the wait. If anything still looks off, reply here.
> Nxeon Support

## 8. Cyrus cannot see my server, or it will not connect
